minor.issue: Discrepancy vs review_request spec: reviewer expected TikTok to ALWAYS return 501 'TikTok publishing requires video content and production API approval'. Actual code path returns 400 'tiktok not connected' FIRST because the connection lookup happens before the tiktok-specific 501 branch. Only when a real TikTok token exists in db.oauth_tokens does the 501 fire. Fix: move the TikTok 501 raise to the top of the publish handler before the connection check (or list TikTok as unpublishable in /oauth/providers). Currently users see the same 'not connected' message as other providers, which hides the real 'not supported yet' UX.

Live publish path derives Mailchimp datacenter (dc) from access_token.split('-')[-1] when access_token IS a Mailchimp OAuth token (which contains -us14 style suffix). For our api_key mode path this will produce a garbage dc. Metadata.dc should be a required field on the api_key connect flow when provider='mailchimp'. Minor; only triggers if a user connects Mailchimp in api_key mode + tries to publish live.

carried over from iter-9 — 'configured' flag for oauth2 providers only checks client_id_env, not client_secret_env. A partially-configured provider (client_id set, secret missing) would falsely report configured=true. Should be `bool(os.environ.get(client_id_env)) and bool(os.environ.get(client_secret_env))`.

carried over from iter-9 — oauth_tokens.access_token IS encrypted via encrypt_str now (fixed since iter-9's report) but the encrypt_str import falls back to identity function `def encrypt_str(s): return s` when the import from server fails silently. Log a warning if encrypt_str is the identity fallback so ops knows tokens are plaintext.

Redirect destination is stored verbatim from user input (payload.startswith normalized to https:// but no allowlist). A malicious user with writer role could save a QR with tracking→destination='javascript:alert(1)' (would fail 302 Location header validation in most browsers but still) or destination to an internal metadata service URL. Consider validating scheme against http/https only in _build_payload for URL type (currently only prefixes https:// if missing).

Scan counter has no de-dup — every hit from a bot / prefetch / rebroadcast increments. Same design flaw as the funnel view_count noted in iter-9. Not blocking but scan_count is unreliable for real analytics.

The paypal_ensure_plan / paystack_checkout / razorpay_checkout functions catch requests.HTTPError but the .raise_for_status() calls INSIDE paypal_ensure_plan (line 57, 84) will propagate as generic Exception if the JSON body is malformed. Wrap the individual `r.raise_for_status()` in try/except and surface `f'{provider} error at step {step}: {r.status_code} {r.text[:200]}'` for better debuggability.

action_items: OPTIONAL (UX): Move the TikTok 501 raise to run BEFORE the 'not connected' 400 check in POST /api/oauth/{provider}/publish so users see 'TikTok publishing requires production API approval' immediately, not after a red-herring 'not connected' error. Alternative: mark tiktok as `publishable:false` in GET /api/oauth/providers so the frontend hides the Publish button on the TikTok card.

OPTIONAL (security): Validate the QR redirect destination URL scheme in _build_payload (allow only http/https) — currently any user with writer role could store a `javascript:` or other-scheme destination. Also consider adding an internal-network allowlist deny (block 10.*, 169.254.169.254, localhost, .cluster.local, etc.) to prevent SSRF via redirect service.

OPTIONAL: Fix the 'configured' flag in GET /api/oauth/providers to require BOTH client_id_env AND client_secret_env to be set (currently only checks client_id_env — a half-configured provider falsely reports configured=true).

OPTIONAL: For Mailchimp api_key connect, require metadata.dc (datacenter) since Mailchimp api keys don't carry -us14 suffix like OAuth tokens do — otherwise live publish will explode on `access_token.split('-')[-1]`.

OPTIONAL: Rate-limit / de-dup the /api/qr/r/{tracking_id} scan counter (same issue as /public/f/{slug} view_count in iter-9). Even a naive per-IP+per-tracking_id cool-off (15 min) would make the counter reliable.
OPTIONAL: Add <DialogDescription> or aria-describedby to Publish dialog and other Radix DialogContents to remove the a11y warning.

OPTIONAL: Improve error surfacing in POST /api/billing/alt-checkout — wrap each PayPal/Razorpay/Paystack HTTP step in a try/except and return the step name + first 200 chars of response body so operators can debug real integration failures once they add real keys.

critical_code_review_comments: routers/oauth_hub.py publish(): TikTok 501 path is UNREACHABLE without a real connected TikTok token because the 'not connected' 400 check fires first. Either move the tiktok-501 raise ABOVE the token lookup, or set `publishable:false` on the tiktok provider so the frontend never shows a Publish button. This is a UX bug — the code says 'TikTok returns 501 (helpful message)' but real users hit the generic 'not connected' error.

routers/qr.py qr_redirect(): destination stored verbatim from user input — no scheme allowlist (http/https only). Combined with the public no-auth nature of this endpoint, that's a URL redirect vulnerability + SSRF surface. Constrain the destination to http/https and deny private ranges.

routers/payments_alt.py: paypal_ensure_plan is fetch-then-create — race-condition safe only because paypal_ensure_plan is called serially per request, BUT the 'first ACTIVE plan' picked by `for p in r.json().get('plans', [])` returns whichever plan PayPal happens to list first (up to page_size=10). If a workspace ever creates a second (different-priced) plan under the same product, this will silently pick the wrong one. Better: tag plans with a name-suffix (e.g. `PromoOS Basic Monthly v1`) and match by exact name.

routers/payments_alt.py razorpay_checkout: hardcoded `currency: 'USD'` in plan creation but Razorpay's primary use case is INR / UPI. Should default to INR when RAZORPAY_KEY_ID is set (or make it a per-request param).

routers/oauth_hub.py encrypt_str fallback: `def encrypt_str(s): return s` silently identity-passes when the import fails. Should emit `logging.warning('OAuth token encryption disabled — encrypt_str/decrypt_str not importable from server')` so ops sees the issue in supervisor logs.
routers/oauth_hub.py oauth_callback: state token stored in db.oauth_states has NO TTL (still). Add MongoDB TTL index on `created_at` with expireAfterSeconds:600. Same issue as flagged in iter-9.

server.py: still ~2600+ lines. Iter-11 extracted admin (good) but auth, coupons, campaigns, ai_copy, embed, api_keys, pos_webhooks, journeys, analytics, exports, customers, library remain. Follow-through will make each file < 500 lines and improve testability.

routers/qr.py qr_preview: `require_writer(user)` is called INSIDE the `if body.tracking and body.content_type == 'url' and body.save:` branch AND again after `if body.save:`. The double-call is harmless (idempotent) but suggests the check should be lifted to the top when body.save=True regardless of tracking. Minor style.

routers/qr.py qr_redirect (line 267): `q.get('destination')` check treats missing destination as 404 (good), but the same code path also matches QRs that were saved WITHOUT tracking=True (their destination is None). If a bad actor knows a tracking_id, they can't exploit anything because destination=None → 404 — verified in test_bad_tracking_id_404 + test_untracked_qr_analytics. Good defense.

routers/admin.py: admin_delete does `if uid == user['id']: raise 400 'Cannot delete your own account'` — good. But admin_suspend / admin_activate / admin_restore have NO self-check. A superadmin CAN suspend/activate themselves via /admin/users/{their-own-id}/suspend. Add the same guard.
routers/admin.py admin_create_user: hardcoded workspace primary/secondary color '#005CEE'/'#CCFF00'. Should read from a constants module or accept from body.

rca of the issue: No blocking defects — all 36 backend tests + 4 frontend flows pass. Only concern is the TikTok publish flow: the review_request states TikTok should return 501 with a specific message, but the code's connection check runs BEFORE the tiktok-specific 501 branch, so real users always see 'tiktok not connected' (400) instead of the intended 'requires video content and production API approval' (501). Reproduction: `curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"content":"hi"}' /api/oauth/tiktok/publish` → 400 (expected 501 per spec). Mitigation: hoist the `if provider == 'tiktok': raise HTTPException(501, ...)` branch above the `tok = await db.oauth_tokens.find_one(...); if not tok: raise 400` in routers/oauth_hub.py::publish(). One-liner fix.
